title: Zeroth Cech set of a covering and the plus construction of a presheaf of sets on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, i.e. a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to$ sets; for $h:V\to W$ write $s\mapsto s|_V=\mathcal F(h)(s)$. (a) *Zeroth Cech set.* For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ put $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\{(s_i)_{i\in I}\in\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\mid s_i|_{U_i\times_UU_j}=s_j|_{U_i\times_UU_j}\ \forall i,j\in I\}$ (restrictions along the two projections of the fibre product), with the canonical map $\mathcal F(U)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $s\mapsto(s|_{U_i})_i$. (b) *Morphisms of coverings.* A morphism (refinement) $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ from $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ to $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to V\}_{j\in J}$ consists of a morphism $\chi:U\to V$, a map $\alpha:I\to J$ and morphisms $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ such that $U_i\xrightarrow{f_i}V_{\alpha(i)}\to V$ equals $U_i\to U\xrightarrow{\chi}V$ for all $i$; it is said to lie over $\chi$. It induces $f^*:H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $(f^*s)_i=s_{\alpha(i)}|_{U_i}$ (restriction along $f_i$), which is well defined because $f_i\times f_{i'}$ maps $U_i\times_UU_{i'}$ to $V_{\alpha(i)}\times_VV_{\alpha(i')}$ compatibly with the projections, and $f^*$ is compatible with $\mathcal F(\chi):\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(U)$ and the canonical maps of (a). A covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$ *refines* a covering $\mathcal V$ of $U$ if there is a morphism $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$. (c) *The plus construction.* Let $\mathcal J_U$ be the category whose objects are the coverings of $U$ and whose morphisms are the morphisms of coverings over $\mathrm{id}_U$ (it is small by the set-theoretic conventions of a site and nonempty, containing $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$); $\mathcal U\mapsto H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $f\mapsto f^*$ is a functor $\mathcal J_U^{opp}\to$ sets. Define $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ (colimit of sets) and write $[\mathcal U,s]\in\mathcal F^+(U)$ for the image of $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$. For a morphism $h:V\to U$, choose for every covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ (axiom (iii) of a site); the covering $\mathcal U\times_UV=\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ and the projections give a morphism of coverings $p_{\mathcal U}:\mathcal U\times_UV\to\mathcal U$ over $h$, natural in $\mathcal U\in\mathcal J_U$, and $\mathcal F^+(h):\mathcal F^+(U)\to\mathcal F^+(V)$ is the induced map of colimits, $[\mathcal U,s]\mapsto[\mathcal U\times_UV,p_{\mathcal U}^*s]$, i.e. $(s_i)\mapsto(s_i|_{U_i\times_UV})$. Finally $\theta_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F^+(U)$, $s\mapsto[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},s]$, using $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$. That these data form a presheaf $\mathcal F^+$ (independent of the choices of fibre products) with a morphism of presheaves $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^+$ is a lemma (Stacks Sites, Lemma 00W4), stated as a node of its own.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (section-sheafification): the definition of $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and of the maps induced by morphisms of coverings, the category $\mathcal J_U$ and $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, the restriction maps via $\mathcal J_U\to\mathcal J_V$, and the map $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F^+(U)$ from the trivial covering; morphisms of coverings as in Sites, Definition 00VT (definition-morphism-coverings)

mathlib_searches.query: plus construction plusObj colimit over covers of the multiequalizer
mathlib_searches.verdict: generalization in another formalism: Mathlib's plus construction is defined for a Grothendieck topology (covering sieves, `J.Cover X`), not for a site given by families of coverings as in Stacks 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the identification of the Stacks plus construction (colimit over coverings) with `plusObj` of the generated topology is itself a theorem (it passes through the topology associated to a site, Stacks Sites, Section 00ZB and Lemma 00ZC, and the sieve-wise construction $L\mathcal F$ of Section 00ZG), so this is not a one-line specialization
